entities.summary:
Estienne de La Roche (1470–1530) was a French mathematician who made significant contributions to the field of astronomy, particularly in the study of celestial mechanics and the calculation of planetary orbits.

La Roche's most notable work is his treatise on the motion of the planets, which was heavily influenced by the works of ancient Greek mathematicians such as Ptolemy and Aristotle. He also developed a new method for calculating the positions of celestial bodies, which was more accurate than existing methods.

La Roche's work had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy, influencing later mathematicians and astronomers such as Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler. His contributions to the field of astronomy helped to lay the foundation for the Scientific Revolution of the 16th and 17th centuries.

As one of the first French mathematicians to make significant contributions to the field of astronomy, La Roche's work represents a key moment in the evolution of scientific knowledge during the Renaissance.
